target_moa.text: Dasatinib is an inhibitor of multiple tyrosine kinases; at nanomolar concentrations it inhibits BCR-ABL, SRC family kinases (SRC, LCK, YES, FYN), c-KIT, EPHA2, and PDGFRβ, and can overcome imatinib resistance from BCR-ABL kinase domain mutations.

citations.quote: SPRYCEL™ (dasatinib) is an inhibitor of multiple tyrosine kinases.
Dasatinib, at nanomolar concentrations, inhibits the following kinases: BCR-ABL, SRC family (SRC, LCK, YES, FYN), c-KIT, EPHA2, and PDGFR\beta.

dasatinib was able to overcome imatinib resistance resulting from BCR-ABL kinase domain mutations, activation of alternate signaling pathways involving the SRC family kinases (LYN, HCK), and multi-drug resistance gene overexpression.
SPRYCEL™ (dasatinib) is an inhibitor of multiple tyrosine kinases.
SPRYCEL tablets are white to off-white, biconvex, film-coated tablets containing dasatinib

key_safety.text: Most common adverse events (≥10%) included fluid retention (50%), diarrhea (49%), headache (40%), hemorrhage (40%), musculoskeletal pain (39%), pyrexia (39%), fatigue (39%). Serious toxicities include severe (Grade 3/4) myelosuppression — neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia — more frequent in advanced CML/Ph+ ALL, and bleeding events (severe CNS hemorrhage in 1%, severe GI hemorrhage in 7%).

Treatment with SPRYCEL is associated with severe (NCI CTC Grade 3 or 4) thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, and anemia.

Severe CNS hemorrhages, including fatalities, occurred in 1% of patients receiving SPRYCEL. Severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage occurred in 7% of patients and generally required treatment interruptions and transfusions.

summary.text: SPRYCEL (NDA 22-072) was submitted December 28, 2005 and approved June 28, 2006 based on hematologic and cytogenetic response rates from four single-arm multicenter studies; the label notes there are no controlled trials demonstrating a clinical benefit such as improved survival, and three postmarketing study commitments were made at approval.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated December 28, 2005, received December 28, 2005, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for SPRYCEL™ (dasatinib) Tablets.

The effectiveness of SPRYCEL is based on hematologic and cytogenetic response rates (see **CLINICAL STUDIES**). There are no controlled trials demonstrating a clinical benefit, such as improvement in disease-related symptoms or increased survival.
We remind you of your postmarketing study commitments in your submission dated June 27, 2006. These commitments are listed below.
